article.title: Comprehensive Email Template Test Article
article.summary: This is a comprehensive test article containing all HTML elements and embed types supported by the email template system. Use this to test template rendering in the admin interface.
article.body:
This is a comprehensive test article designed to showcase all HTML structural elements and embed types that can appear in email templates. This article includes every possible content type to help test template rendering in the admin interface.

All Heading Levels

This section demonstrates all six heading levels:

Heading Level 1 (H1)

Content following an H1 heading.

Heading Level 2 (H2)

Content following an H2 heading.

Heading Level 3 (H3)

Content following an H3 heading.

Heading Level 4 (H4)

Content following an H4 heading.

Heading Level 5 (H5)

Content following an H5 heading.

Heading Level 6 (H6)

Content following an H6 heading.

Text Formatting and Inline Elements

This paragraph contains bold text, italic text, underlined text, and regular links. You can also find tokenized links that will be processed by the template system.

Additional inline elements: HTML, The Art of Web Design, code snippets, deleted text, inserted text, highlighted text, small text, subscript, superscript, January 15, 2024, variable, Ctrl+C, and sample output.

Links can have titles: link with title.

Paragraphs can contain multiple lines of text and should render properly with appropriate spacing and line heights as defined in the newsletter.css stylesheet. This paragraph demonstrates proper line wrapping and spacing between paragraphs.

Empty paragraphs should be handled gracefully.

Paragraphs with only whitespace should also be handled.

    Conclusion

    This comprehensive test article includes all structural HTML elements that could appear in an article body. It covers:

    • All heading levels (h1-h6)
    • All text formatting and inline elements
    • All list types (ul, ol, dl) including nested lists
    • Various table structures
    • Blockquotes in various configurations
    • Images and figures in multiple contexts
    • Code blocks and inline code
    • Horizontal rules
    • Footnotes with proper structure
    • Container elements (div, span)
    • Address elements
    • Complex nested structures
    • Edge cases and special characters

    This article should help verify that all HTML elements and embed types are properly processed and rendered in email templates when testing template render calls in the admin interface.
